question.text: What is the maximum allocation that a single allottee can receive in a Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP)?

answer.text: Not more than 50% of the QIP issue size
Not more than 10% of the QIP issue size
Not more than 25% of the QIP issue size

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI ICDR provides that no single allottee in a QIP shall be allotted more than 50% of the issue size. This concentration cap ensures that a QIP does not become a single-investor placement disguised as an institutional one. The Trap: "No cap" is wrong because the 50% concentration limit always applies. The 10% and 25% figures sound regulatory but are not the QIP single-allottee ceiling. Note: A QIP also requires a minimum number of allottees, and at least 10% of the issue must be allotted to mutual funds (with the unallotted MF portion flowing back to other QIBs if undersubscribed).
